cards.text: This one's a psalm of Asaph, one of the Levites David appointed to lead worship (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). He's in trouble, and he cries out to God. Not in a whisper either: he cries ALOUD, so God will hear him.
In the day of trouble, Asaph seeks the Lord. All through the night his hands stay outstretched, and they don't grow weary.

cards.question: In his day of trouble, how does Asaph's soul respond to comfort?

cards.text: Then Asaph remembers God, right in the middle of his trouble.

cards.question: When Asaph remembers God in his trouble, what happens to him?

answers.text: He groans and his spirit grows faint
He sings and his spirit grows strong
He rests and his spirit grows calm

cards.text: And sleep? Asaph tells God, "You have kept my eyes from closing." So now Asaph's up all night, supervising the ceiling.

cards.question: Up all night, Asaph is so ___ that he can't even speak.

cards.text: Then Asaph thinks back to the days of old, the years long in the past. At night he remembers his song, and his spirit starts asking some hard questions.

cards.question: In the night, Asaph's spirit starts asking hard questions. What does he ask might go on forever?

answers.text: His own nights without any sleep

cards.question: In his questions, Asaph even wonders if God's promise has failed for all time.
Asaph asks if God has forgotten to be gracious. Then he asks if God's anger has shut off His ___.
After all those questions, Asaph sums up his grief in one line. What does he say has changed?

answers.text: The right hand of the Most High
The hearts of the people of Israel
The song he sang in the night

cards.text: Then the psalm turns. Asaph quits supervising the ceiling and makes up his mind.

cards.question: After all his hard questions, what does Asaph decide he will remember?
Asaph plans to take a quick glance at what God has done and move right along.

cards.text: Asaph tells God, "Your way, O God, is holy." Friend, a few verses ago this man was too troubled to speak. Now he can't STOP.

cards.question: Asaph asks, What god is so great as our God? What is he saying with that question?

answers.text: No god is as great as his God
Some other god may be greater
He isn't sure who God really is

cards.text: He calls God the God who works wonders, the One who shows His strength among the peoples.

cards.question: Asaph says God redeemed His people with power. Who are they?

answers.text: The sons of Jacob and Joseph
The sons of Moab and Ammon
The sons of Esau and Ishmael

cards.text: That's Jacob, also called Israel (Genesis 35:10), and Joseph, one of his twelve sons (Genesis 35:22-24). Now Asaph paints one of God's wonders, and it begins with water.

cards.question: In Asaph's picture, what do the waters do when they see God?

answers.text: They swirl and even the depths shake
They freeze and the depths stand still
They rise and cover the whole land

cards.text: Then the sky joins in. The clouds pour down water, thunder resounds, and God's arrows flash back and forth.

cards.question: With God's thunder resounding in the whirlwind, the earth stays perfectly still.

cards.text: The lightning lights up the world, and the earth trembles and quakes. Me? Back when I was stuck in a junk drawer, I'd jump every time somebody rattled it looking for TAPE.

cards.question: Asaph says God's path led through the mighty waters, yet His footprints were never found.
God's footprints can't be found, but He still leads. How does He lead His people?

answers.text: Like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron
Like an army by the hand of Joshua and Caleb
Like a nation by the hand of David and Solomon

cards.text: Moses and Aaron, the two the LORD told to bring the Israelites out of Egypt (Exodus 6:26). And right there, Asaph lets his song come to rest.
